A directory tree is a "micro-tree" when its regular files add up to less than `micro_tree_max_bytes`, which is 2 * 1024 * 1024 bytes (2 MiB) (src/main.zig:38-42).

When it is one, zgrep takes a zero-thread fast path (src/main.zig:38-40):
- The tree is scanned on the calling thread, with no thread pool.
- The upward `.dataignore`/`.gitignore` walk is skipped.

Passing `--force-swarm` opts out and restores the concurrent swarm (src/main.zig:41). The threshold is passed into the kamikaze call along with `opts.force_swarm` (src/main.zig:2452-2453).

The context doesn't show the code that measures the tree size or implements the fast path, so I can't say how the sum is computed (e.g., whether it stops early) or whether the comparison is strictly "less than" in code beyond what the comment states.
